briefings.title: Adam Foroughi, Applovin CEO: Surviving a 92% Drawdown, Ads as ML 1.0 & the $50B Game Ad Market
briefings.tldr: AppLovin CEO Adam Foroughi details how the mobile gaming ad network transformed from a regression model to a deep learning engine, generating roughly $6 billion in cash this year with 84% EBITDA margins by successfully scaling performance-based advertising and aggressive share buybacks.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AppLovin CEO Adam Foroughi details how the mobile gaming ad network transformed from a regression model to a deep learning engine, generating roughly $6 billion in cash this year with 84% EBITDA margins by successfully scaling performance-based advertising and aggressive share buybacks.

## Company Overview & Market Dynamics
* **Core Business Model:** AppLovin operates as an ad platform monetizing mobile game developers, helping them match users with relevant content and driving app-to-app intent.
* **Massive Market Scale:** 
  * Over 1 billion adults play mobile casual games daily.
  * The mobile gaming ad spend market is estimated at roughly **$50 billion** annually.
  * AppLovin's platform platform ad spend grew 60% year-over-year from a baseline disclosed nearly two years ago of $11 billion.
* **Expansion into E-Commerce:** Deep learning models have advanced to the point where AppLovin can take adult gamers and deliver shopper behavior experiences, tapping into much larger economies.

## Advertising & Machine Learning Evolution
* **ML 1.0:** Advertising served as the original implementation of deep learning models and recommendation systems, laying the groundwork for modern AI trajectories.
* **Discovery vs. Search:** 
  * Bottom-funnel search advertising (like Google) competes where consumer intent is already established.
  * Discovery advertising (used by Meta and AppLovin) creates intent for products consumers didn't know existed, generating genuine economic expansion and GDP growth.
* **Privacy & Ad Relevance:** Despite privacy rule changes (such as Apple's tracking restrictions) and initial user resistance, technology adapted via deep learning to serve relevant ads that consumers engage with via rewards and previews.

## Financial Turnaround & Capital Allocation
* **The 2021–2023 Tumble:** 
  * AppLovin went public in April 2021 at a **$28 billion** market cap ($600M EBITDA).
  * Due to supply overhang from private investors and lack of blue-chip research during the SPAC/IPO boom, the stock plummeted to a **$3.8 billion** market cap in 2022 despite generating **$1 billion** in EBITDA that year.
* **Becoming Their Own Best Investor:** 
  * Realizing the market was mispricing the business, Foroughi halted investor relations and launched an aggressive buyback program.
  * The company bought roughly **$6 billion** of its own stock, retiring 20% to 25% of shares outstanding.
* **The Re-engagement Surge:** When Foroughi returned to New York to meet investors in September 2023 after launching an ML 2.0 deep learning model in April 2023, the stock jumped from $80 to $150 in a single week.

## Operating Strategy, Margins & Global Engineering
* **Lean Execution:** Maintaining a lean, hyper-focused team of subject matter experts allows AppLovin to move faster than tech giants.
* **Margin Profile:** AppLovin boasts an industry-leading **84% EBITDA margin**, driven by automated, algorithmically focused performance arbitrage where advertisers cover consumer acquisition costs immediately upon transaction.
* **Global Talent Footprint:** Engineering offices are distributed across Palo Alto, Singapore, and Beijing, tapping into elite, hardworking international engineering talent.

## Notable Quotes
> *"In a world where things don't make sense, people think you're cheating, instead of realizing you built one of the cooler technologies the world's ever seen."* — **Adam Foroughi**

> *"Your price in the markets is determined by the quality of your investors... I turned internal to the team and said, 'I'm not going to talk to investors at all anymore. They're not buying our stock. It's a waste of time. But guess what? We generated a ton of cash. Let's start buying our own stock.'"* — **Adam Foroughi**

> *"We never think we won. We think every day we wake up and we're probably going to get screwed right now and we better work hard."* — **Adam Foroughi**

briefings.title: Brad Gerstner "$4 trillion of wealth transfer to kids who would've otherwise had zero"
briefings.tldr: Brad Gerstner, Founder of Invest America, outlines the rapid scaling of Trump Accounts to 70 million American children, aiming to inject $4 trillion in wealth transfer over 10 years to kids who would otherwise have zero.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
Brad Gerstner, Founder of Invest America, outlines the rapid scaling of Trump Accounts to 70 million American children, aiming to inject $4 trillion in wealth transfer over 10 years to kids who would otherwise have zero.

### Program Scale and Current Metrics
* **Current Account Volume:** **9 million accounts** already created today, making it one of the largest programs in federal government history.
* **Seed Funding and Philanthropic Contributions:** 
  * **$6.25 billion** committed by **Michael & Susan Dell** to fund $250 investment account deposits for 25 million U.S. children aged 10 and under.
  * **Up to $100 million** personally pledged by **Brad Gerstner** for children in Indiana, with funds hitting accounts starting on a Thursday.
  * **$1,000 federal seed** allocated for eligible newborns.
* **Corporate Integration:** Companies nationwide are incorporating Trump Accounts into standard 401(k) infrastructure (which commands $75 billion a year in inflows and $15 trillion in total assets).

### Platform Design and Financial Literacy
* **Frictionless UX:** The app enables instant peer-to-peer contributions via Apple Pay and debit cards using QR code scans, customizable messages, and photos.
* **Educational Wrappers:** In Texas, financial literacy programs are being paired with Trump Accounts for 750,000 kids, utilizing the app's interactive savings slider to teach compounding.
* **Overcoming the Cold Start:** **Brad Gerstner** emphasizes that the program solves the hardest financial hurdle—moving from zero to one—to connect lower-income Americans directly with capital ownership and the American dream.

### Bipartisan Backing and Government Execution
* **Cross-Party Support:** Despite political polarization, the initiative has secured bipartisan backing from figures including Senators Booker, Warner, Cruz, Hagerty, and Thune, alongside endorsements from Gavin Newsom and Bill Clinton.
* **Executive Push:** **Brad Gerstner** notes that President Trump immediately championed the initiative as the core of his "Main Street agenda" and coordinated directly with the Speaker of the House to pass legislation.
* **Key Implementers:** **Brad Gerstner** credited program execution partners including Scott Bessent, Frank Bisignano (managing the IRS, Social Security, and Trump Accounts), and private sector partners like Michael Dell, Joe Gebbia, and Vlad Tenev.

### Predictions & Forward Calls
* **70M Account Milestone:** **Brad Gerstner** forecasts that Trump Accounts will expand to 70 million accounts within 30 days, serving as the official programmatic "IPO."
* **10-Year Wealth Target:** **Brad Gerstner** forecasts that within the next 10 years, Trump Accounts will hold **$4 trillion** in wealth transfer for children.
* **25-Year Projection:** **Brad Gerstner** predicts that over the next 25 years, these accounts will grow to **$10 trillion to $20 trillion**, engaging a generation of 150 million Americans in the economic system.

### Notable Quotes
> "This is $4 trillion of wealth transfer to kids who would've otherwise had zero, who feel like they're totally out of the game, like they're not part of the American dream."
> — **Brad Gerstner**

> "The hardest movement in life is from zero to one. It's getting into the game. It's overcoming the cold start problem... Once you're on first base, getting to second base is easier."
> — **Brad Gerstner**

briefings.title: Extended interview: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on fears about AI
briefings.tldr: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argues that doomsday fears about artificial intelligence are dramatic and irresponsible distractions, emphasizing that the AI industry is simply transitioning from research labs to high-production product companies that must prioritize engineering safety under existing laws rather than new regulations.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argues that doomsday fears about artificial intelligence are dramatic and irresponsible distractions, emphasizing that the AI industry is simply transitioning from research labs to high-production product companies that must prioritize engineering safety under existing laws rather than new regulations.

## Industry Transition from Research Labs to Production
* **Shift to Product Focus:** Jensen Huang notes that top AI companies have spent the past 10-15 years as research labs and are now shifting into high production ramp mode to meet massive global demand.
* **Token Generation Profitability:** AI token generation products have become incredibly profitable, leading to widespread adoption by companies such as OpenAI (Astra), Cloud Code, Cursor, SpaceX, and Cognition.
* **Engineering Priority Shift:** Just as the aviation industry matured to dedicate more engineering to verification and safety than building new aircraft, AI companies are necessarily shifting compute and researchers toward security sandboxes, isolation, containment, and testing.

## Safety, Regulation, and the Rule of Law
* **Rejection of Doomsday Narratives:** Huang dismisses claims that AI will end humanity within a decade as false, ungrounded in science, and "irresponsible" drama designed for attention or ulterior motives.
* **Sufficiency of Existing Laws:** Rather than calling for new AI-specific laws or an FDA/FAA equivalent for AI, Huang insists that current product liability and cybersecurity laws should be applied first.
* **Critique of Safety Advocates:** Huang suggests that prominent lab CEOs calling for regulation may actually be seeking relief from existing legal liabilities rather than genuine oversight.
* **Empathy for First-Time CEOs:** Huang expresses confidence in young, first-time tech leaders like Dario Amodei and Sam Altman, acknowledging the immense pressure of their rapid transition from research labs to businesses generating tens or hundreds of billions in revenue.

## The Geopolitical Race with China and Global Strategy
* **Need for Domestic Speed:** Huang advises that America should go "as fast as we can" in AI development to maximize economic prosperity, national security, and philanthropic capability.
* **Disagreement on Chip Bans:** Huang explicitly disagrees with Dario Amodei's recommendation to block sales of powerful AI chips to China, arguing that American companies should lead with advanced technology (such as the volume-producing Vera Rubin chips, which are years ahead of China) before competing in the global market.
* **Value of Global Collaboration:** In upcoming talks with President Xi Jinping, Huang intends to advocate for shared best practices and global product safety standards while leaving military and national security boundaries to governments.

## The Reindustrialization of America via AI Factories
* **AI as Digital Intelligence Manufacturing:** Huang reframes data centers as "AI factories" that ingest energy and data to manufacture digital intelligence ("tokens").
* **Economic Boost for Blue-Collar Workers:** These data center buildouts represent the first major reindustrialization of the United States in decades, creating massive demand and prosperity for construction workers, electricians, and blue-collar trades.
* **Addressing Community Backlash:** Acknowledging that data centers appeared too quickly in rural areas without sufficient community dialogue, Huang stresses the need for better upfront engagement, improved aesthetics, and contributions to local energy grids and community investments.
* **Debunking Resource Myths:** Huang clarifies that modern data center cooling uses recirculating hot water (less evaporative water consumption than a backyard swimming pool) and that data center investments ultimately enhance grid reliability and lower energy costs.

## Taxes, Philanthropy, and Personal Perspective
* **Support for Wealth Taxes:** Unlike some peers, Huang states he is completely fine paying higher taxes (such as California's proposed Proposition 40), viewing his ability to pay billions in taxes as a privilege of the American dream.
* **Gratitude for the American System:** Reflecting on his early days as a dishwasher at Denny's in Onita, Kentucky, Huang credits meritocracy, grit, and the U.S. educational and economic system for Nvidia's success.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Sustained Fossil Fuel Usage:** Huang states that over the next 5 years, data centers and AI expansion will undoubtedly use much more fossil fuel energy.
* **Transition to Sustainable Energy:** Huang predicts that in the decades following the immediate 5-year buildout, AI market forces will drive the widespread application and adoption of sustainable energy sources (including solar, hydro, and nuclear fusion/fission).
* **Multi-Trillion Dollar Industry Growth:** Huang predicts that AI factories and digital intelligence infrastructure will become a multi-trillion-dollar industry touching every part of the economy.

## Notable Quotes
> "Any anything all the messaging around the drama of it is unnecessary. It is is quite frankly uh too much drama irresponsible. It is now grounded on facts. It's not grounded on science." — Jensen Huang

> "The fact that I can afford to pay $8 billion in taxes over five years is a privilege. It's not that it it's not the $8 billion. It's the fact that I can afford to pay $8 billion... I'm not afraid of paying taxes. I'm just afraid of being poor." — Jensen Huang

> "We want America to be as prosperous as we can. The more prosperous we are, the richer we are as an economy, the more we could provide for social security, the more we could provide for national military security... I would advise that every single American citizen, everybody in America pulls in the same direction as hard as we can." — Jensen Huang

briefings.title: Howard Marks Flags the Uncertainty in AI Investing
briefings.tldr: Markets have been dominated by optimists driven by strong economic aggregates, the TINA trade, and AI enthusiasm, though this requires heightened investor caution.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Markets have been dominated by optimists driven by strong economic aggregates, the TINA trade, and AI enthusiasm, though this requires heightened investor caution. While AI's transformative potential is undeniable, extreme uncertainty surrounding future profitability and societal impact makes it impossible to definitively label current market exuberance as irrational.

## The Macro Environment & Market Psychology
- **Federal Reserve Communication:** Howard Marks argues that less central bank communication is preferable, as it forces businesses and portfolios to become antifragile rather than relying entirely on Fed projections.
  - Expresses a personal preference for a less activist central bank that lets the free market determine natural interest rates through borrower-lender negotiations unless the economy is heading off the rails.
- **Optimism-Driven Markets:** Markets have been ruled by optimists since roughly October 1, 2022, with the S&P 500 more than doubling in that period.
  - The S&P surge is supported by positive underlying truths, including a US economy that performs as the best-developed world economy, the "TINA" (there is no alternative) trade, and AI excitement.
  - Marks attributes persistent optimism partly to the absence of a truly severe downturn since the global financial crisis market bottom in March 2009, leading people to extrapolate good times.
  - When optimists are in charge, they slough off bad news and react positively to settlement rumors without getting depressed when deals fall through, creating a positive market bias that calls for built-in defense and caution.

## AI Investment & Valuation Challenges
- **The Definition of Value Investing:** Marks defines his approach as a "small v" value investor whose goal is to calculate an asset's intrinsic value and buy it at a fair price relative to that value.
- **The "Too Hard" Pile:** Evaluating pure-play AI companies is extremely challenging because they may not have produced profits yet, making it difficult to quantify earnings potential 5 years out.
  - Hyperscalers like Microsoft and Amazon have supporting legacy businesses, but companies all-in on AI present an unusual degree of uncertainty for intrinsic valuation, fitting Warren Buffett's description of the "too hard pile."
- **Exuberance vs. Irrationality:** Alan Greenspan's 1997 phrase "irrational exuberance" defines a bubble, and while AI exuberance is undeniable, Marks hesitates to label it definitively as irrational.
  - Because nobody can definitively scope what AI will accomplish, its profitability, or its broader effects, nobody can prove the exuberance is irrational.
  - The presence of uncertainty does not mean investors should do nothing, but it must be acknowledged to properly inform investment sizing and strategy.

## Societal Impact & Government Policy
- **Existential Economic Concerns:** Marks previously warned about the acute societal ramifications of AI displacing workers in Middle America and across the country.
  - Reiterates that sentient human beings must acknowledge these risks, though he notes his wife defines worrying as "bleeding before you're shot" since individuals cannot personally stop the trend.
- **Policy Vacuum:** Marks criticizes the lack of government foresight, stating there should be a dedicated task force examining the coming effects of AI.
  - Poses a critical unanswered fiscal question for policymakers: If AI replaces human workers, will it replace them as taxpayers, and what will happen to government revenues when people lose their jobs?

## Corporate Integration & Critical Thinking
- **Enterprise Usage at Oaktree:** Oaktree Capital Management uses AI internally to marshal data and perform early analysis on tasks that used to take a long time, but has not turned business or investment decisions over to algorithms.
  - Exceptional investing does not come from computers, but from a superior ability to assess the import of data—a superiority AI does not yet possess.
- **Preserving Cognitive Muscles:** Oaktree does not encourage younger hires to outsource critical thinking to AI.
  - Stopping critical thinking causes individuals to "lose the muscle," and the ultimate edge in investing remains fundamentally human.
  - Marks compares AI's disruptive potential to indexation in equity investing—putting many active investors out of business, but not the best.

## Notable Quotes
> *"When society thinks—when everybody in society thinks they know exactly what the Fed's gonna do and prepares for that, then the society is dependent on that outcome. And if if if something else happens, then, you know, bad things can happen."* — **Howard Marks**

> *"My wife defines worrying as bleeding before you're shot. And in this case, there's nothing we can do about it. Nothing certainly nothing I can do about it personally. So, you roll with it."* — **Howard Marks**

> *"If people are put out of work, they won't pay taxes. If AI takes their place as as workers, will it take their place as taxpayers and how? So what will happen to government revenues when when and if people lose their jobs?"* — **Howard Marks**

briefings.title: IMF MD on the Global Economic Outlook
briefings.tldr: Global economic growth is proving resilient at around 3%, supported by positive AI demand and emerging market strength, but faces persistent risks from sticky inflation, rising debt-servicing costs, and AI-driven financial stability concerns.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Global economic growth is proving resilient at around 3%, supported by positive AI demand and emerging market strength, but faces persistent risks from sticky inflation, rising debt-servicing costs, and AI-driven financial stability concerns.

## Global Economic Outlook & Shocks
- **Growth Resiliency:** The global economy is hovering around 3% GDP growth, a massive achievement despite ongoing shocks, though projections will be revised to reflect high ongoing risks.
- **Opposing Forces:** Two main drivers are pushing in opposite directions:
  - A negative energy supply shock holding the economy back.
  - A positive AI investment demand shock lifting the economy up.
- **Emerging Market Strength:** Emerging markets and developing economies have built strong institutional buffers and monetary policy frameworks that match or exceed advanced economies.

## Inflation, Debt, and Fiscal Pressures
- **Persistent Inflation:** Inflation is stable but not resolving quickly, requiring central banks (including in Europe and the US) to maintain or increase tightening.
- **Climbing Debt-Servicing Costs:** Higher interest rates have increased debt-servicing burdens, making fiscal consolidation essential.
- **US Fiscal Deficits:** US debt levels have climbed to over $40 trillion, and while relying on growth to reduce debt is a strategy, the IMF advocates for gradually bringing deficits down.
- **Low-Income Country Debt:** The IMF is engaging in debt restructuring discussions—notably using a new playbook for Senegal—and utilizing the Global Sovereign Debt Roundtable to coordinate traditional, new, and private creditors.
- **Argentina's Transition:** Argentina has successfully moved from deficit to surplus and brought inflation down; the focus must now shift to translating macroeconomic stability into growth and employment.

## AI Risks and Energy Security
- **Financial Stability Front-Loading:** High expectations for AI create risks of front-loaded financial instability, circular financing, and leverage vulnerabilities if expectations are disappointed.
- **Global Value Chain Exposure:** US-centric AI concentration impacts integrated value chains globally, with visible stock market vulnerabilities in Korea and critical production in the Netherlands, Malaysia, Thailand, and Singapore.
- **Surging Energy Consumption:** AI is already consuming 3% of energy in Europe, and consumption is projected to triple by the end of the decade, making energy security critical.
- **Energy Shock Mitigations:** The 2025 energy shock was sustained through rapid responses:
  - Nigeria and India expanded refinery capacity quickly.
  - The US and Norway increased production.
  - Saudi Arabia and the UAE provided alternative routes around the Strait of Hormuz.
  - European renewables and reduced energy intensity helped absorb the shock.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **AI Energy Consumption Growth:** AI energy consumption will become three times higher by the end of the decade — Kristalina Georgieva.
- **Mid-October Forecast Revisions:** The IMF will release new global projections in mid-October that reflect continued high risks to the global economy — Kristalina Georgieva.

## Notable Quotes
> "The risks are high and uncertainty is the new normal."
> — Kristalina Georgieva

> "We always overestimate the positive impact of new technology in the short run. We underestimate it in the long run. What does it mean? It means that risks are front loaded."
> — Kristalina Georgieva

briefings.title: LNG Damage May Take Years to Repair Qatar Says

people.name: Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani

briefings.tldr: Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani reports that regional conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruptions have caused a 7% economic contraction and wiped out 17% of Qatar's revenues, with LNG facility damages requiring an estimated two to three years to repair.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani reports that regional conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruptions have caused a 7% economic contraction and wiped out 17% of Qatar's revenues, with LNG facility damages requiring an estimated two to three years to repair. Despite these pressures, strong fiscal buffers—including a drop in debt-to-GDP from 60% to 40% and 3.5% growth in the non-hydrocarbon sector—have allowed the Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) to maintain its global investment strategy, particularly in technology and AI.

## Impact of Regional Conflict on Qatar's Economy
* **Revenue and Growth Shocks:** 
  * **17% Revenue Loss:** Disruption in the Strait of Hormuz and regional conflict between the US and Iran have placed severe pressure on energy prices and state revenues.
  * **7% GDP Contraction:** The broader economy contracted due to the war, driven entirely by the hydrocarbon sector.
* **Non-Hydrocarbon Resilience:** 
  * **3.5% Growth:** The non-hydrocarbon economy grew despite the crisis, driven by ongoing national economic diversification.
  * **GDP Contribution Shift:** The non-hydrocarbon share of GDP rose from 40% in 2011 to 70% recently.
* **Fiscal Buffers and Ratings:** 
  * **Debt Reduction:** The government successfully reduced its debt-to-GDP ratio from 60% to 40%.
  * **Credit Rating:** Qatar maintains an affirmed double-A country rating alongside large reserves in the central bank.
  * **Stabilization Fund:** Surpluses accumulated during good years have created a stabilization fund to support the government, meaning the state has not yet needed to draw financial support from the QIA.

## LNG Infrastructure Damage and Expansion Plans
* **Repair Timeline:** 
  * **2 to 3 Years:** Initial estimations indicate that repairing the heavily attacked LNG facilities will take two to three years.
* **Production Expansion Targets:** 
  * **Phase 1 Launch in 2027:** The first phase of a major new production expansion is scheduled to start producing in 2027, though timelines remain dependent on the situation in the Strait of Hormuz and regional developments.
  * **145 Million Tons by 2030:** The expansion is designed to double production capacity to reach 145 million tons per year by 2030.

## Global Investment Strategy and AI Focus
* **QIA Global Deployment:** 
  * **No Domestic Restriction:** Despite regional conflict, QIA has not shifted to a purely domestic focus and continues to fulfill global investment commitments.
  * **US Market Focus:** The largest portion of QIA's portfolio is deployed in the United States due to its deep capital markets and high concentration of innovation.
  * **Neutrality:** QIA does not pick sides in the competition between Chinese AI and American AI, focusing instead on long-term profitability and value creation for future generations.
* **Technology and Artificial Intelligence:** 
  * **Diversified Portfolio:** QIA maintains a diversified long-term portfolio rather than a single-sector focus, but technology and AI represent major areas of current investment.

## Central Bank Operations and Regulation
* **AI Implementation in Government:** 
  * **18 Central Bank Projects:** The Qatar Central Bank currently has 18 AI projects underway, with 4 already delivered.
  * **Efficiency Gains:** The deployed AI tools have reduced operational costs and accelerated processing times.
* **Regulatory Approach:** 
  * **Pro-Regulation Stance:** The governor is a strong proponent of government regulation to govern AI safely.
  * **Protection Over Restriction:** Guardrails must be designed to protect technology and benefit everyone rather than slow down technological development.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **LNG Repair Timeline:** Repairing the damaged LNG facilities will take two to three years — Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani (First estimation).
* **Expansion Production Start:** The first phase of the new LNG production expansion will start by 2027, depending on regional developments — Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani.
* **Maximum Production Target:** Qatar will reach a maximum production capacity of 145 million tons of LNG a year by 2030 — Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani.

## Notable Quotes
> "LNG facility has been attacked. The damage is huge and will take, as per the first estimation, like, two to three years to repair. However, the good news is that, you know, we've been working on the a new expansion, a new expansion that will, double our size of a production, and we will reach 145,000,000 tons a year by 2030."
> — Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani

> "We are not picky, and we look to all the options in in in a place. However, most of our investments the largest portfolio of QIA is deployed in United States Of America because most of the innovation and the deep capital market is in The United States Of America."
> — Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani

> "I'm a believer of regulation... AI is important. It's the future, and we support this technology. We support the development of this technology, but we have to have a regulation, in place."
> — Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani

briefings.title: Qatar, Brookfield on Trade, Investment and Competition

people.name: Faisal bin Thani bin Faisal Al-Thani

briefings.tldr: Despite global uncertainties and regional instability, Qatar continues to maintain strong GDP growth and attract record foreign investment, while partnerships like Brookfield and the Qatar Investment Authority are scaling up local AI infrastructure and energy-to-compute projects.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Despite global uncertainties and regional instability, Qatar continues to maintain strong GDP growth and attract record foreign investment, while partnerships like Brookfield and the Qatar Investment Authority are scaling up local AI infrastructure and energy-to-compute projects.

## Economic Resilience and Stability in Qatar
* **Long-Term Regional Growth:** 
  * H.E. Sheikh Faisal bin Thani bin Faisal Al-Thani noted that Qatar has achieved 6% year-over-year GDP growth across the past decade despite facing multiple crises including Covid-19, oil price crashes, and regional instability.
  * Bruce Flatt described the development in the Middle East and Qatar over the past 25 years as "almost a miracle," noting that capital availability and a push for system resilience will drive significant investments over the next 15 years.
* **Ground-Level Business Activity:** 
  * In the three months following the onset of the recent conflict, over 5,000 new foreign-owned companies were established in Qatar, representing a 60% increase compared to the same period last year.
  * Local Qatari manufacturers increased their exports by 12% over the same timeframe.
  * H.E. Sheikh Faisal noted that active discussions are ongoing with international firms to relocate regional offices or expand operations, representing at least $15 billion of foreign direct investment (FDI) with plans remaining unchanged.

## $20B AI Infrastructure and Compute Partnership
* **Energy-to-Compute Transition:** 
  * Brookfield and the Qatar Investment Authority (QIA / Chi-I) formed a $20 billion joint venture in December to focus on artificial intelligence infrastructure.
  * Bruce Flatt highlighted that Qatar's abundant natural gas allows the country to convert local energy directly into compute services, creating high-margin economic value.
* **Global Demand for Localized Compute:** 
  * Data centers are being commissioned and construction will start shortly to sell compute both domestically—as every country requires local AI capacity—and internationally.
  * Bruce Flatt noted that global data storage and intelligence are shifting away from being exclusively centralized in the United States toward local country build-outs due to domestic capacity constraints.
* **Agnostic Supplier Strategy:** 
  * H.E. Sheikh Faisal stated that Qatar and Brookfield remain agnostic regarding technology suppliers, utilizing both Chinese and American technology based on customer demand (such as building identical neighboring data centers in the Maldives and Indonesia using different national technologies).
  * Bruce Flatt observed that the global market is developing into parallel systems—a Chinese-led system and a Western/US-led system—operating independently.

## Investment Strategy and Public-Private Collaboration
* **Core Investment Rules:** 
  * Bruce Flatt outlined Brookfield’s 40-year investment philosophy: pick the right countries (operating in roughly 30 nations including the US, UK, France, Australia, Canada, Brazil, and Colombia), partner with good people, and buy or build good backbone infrastructure.
  * Brookfield manages approximately $700 billion of investments in the United States and is a major infrastructure investor across the globe.
* **Domestic Policy and KPIs:** 
  * H.E. Sheikh Faisal explained that while QIA is a financial institution prioritizing financial returns, resilience metrics (such as food, medical, and manufacturing security) serve as positive considerations under Qatar's National Development Strategy (which features eight key pillars, including manufacturing).

## Value of Global Institutions and Dialogue
* **Continued Relevancy:** 
  * H.E. Sheikh Faisal emphasized that international gatherings like the UN General Assembly and G20 remain essential because they maintain channels for dialogue, even among opponents.
  * Bruce Flatt agreed on the value of global meetings, noting that despite event fatigue, human commonalities make regular dialogue a positive force for stability.

## Notable Quotes
> *"What's gone on in the Middle East and what has been achieved in that 25 year period is almost a miracle. In fact, it's one of the two miracles in the world done completed in the last 25 years."* — **Bruce Flatt**

> *"The biggest impediment to bringing on more compute, more artificial intelligence in the world is power... Qatar is very, very in a fortunate situation. They have a lot of gas. And if we can convert local energy into compute, it's hugely the margins are enormously valuable to the country."* — **Bruce Flatt**

> *"We believe in dialogue. And as long as institutions like this open the door for people to be able to meet, even when opponents are able to sit in the same room and have a dialogue, then I think they will always have a place."* — **H.E. Sheikh Faisal bin Thani bin Faisal Al-Thani**

briefings.title: Qatar, Citi and PIMCO on Capital Discipline and Resilience
briefings.tldr: Leaders from Qatar, Citi, and PIMCO discuss navigating the economic shocks of the regional conflict that began in February 2026, highlighting Qatar's fiscal discipline, a global surge in AI-driven energy demand, and structural shifts in international trade and capital allocation.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Leaders from Qatar, Citi, and PIMCO discuss navigating the economic shocks of the regional conflict that began in February 2026, highlighting Qatar's fiscal discipline, a global surge in AI-driven energy demand, and structural shifts in international trade and capital allocation.

## Qatar’s Fiscal Resilience and Economic Strategy
* **Financial Impact of the Conflict:** 
  * **H.E. Ali bin Ahmed Al-Kuwari:** Noted that halted oil and gas exports (representing nearly 70% of revenues) caused a first-half budget deficit of **$36 billion** and a Q1 GDP contraction of **7%** (with oil and gas down **25%**, though non-oil grew **3.5%**).
* **Fiscal Tightening and Debt Management:**
  * **Operational Efficiency:** Second-quarter expenditures were reduced by **25%** compared to the same period last year through operational tightening.
  * **Debt Reduction:** Despite the crisis, Qatar settled **$5.5 billion** in debt, including a **$3 million** private placement. Debt-to-GDP was successfully reduced from **70%** post-COVID to **42%**.
  * **Credit Ratings:** Qatar's credit ratings were affirmed by all three major rating agencies, maintaining a **double-A** status.
* **Sovereign Investment Restructuring:**
  * **Mandate Split:** The Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) is splitting its focus: QIA will continue international investments and diversification, while a newly established platform will focus on the local economy, startups, new sectors, and the National Development Strategy 3 (expiring in **2030**).

## Global Energy Pressures, AI Infrastructure, and Capital Demands
* **Energy Bottlenecks and Inflationary Risks:**
  * **Jane Fraser:** Highlighted that rising diesel and refined product prices, compounded by Ukrainian actions reducing Russian capacity, point toward a bumpier road for inflation.
  * **Emmanuel Roman:** Noted that AI compute demand has shifted the primary technology bottleneck from chips into energy, creating real, multi-year global demand.
* **AI Financing and Structural Shifts:**
  * **PIMCO Deals:** Emmanuel Roman highlighted PIMCO’s involvement in massive data center financing deals, including with Oracle in Michigan and Meta in Louisiana.
  * **Exporting Computational Power:** H.E. Ali bin Ahmed Al-Kuwari emphasized that Qatar views AI as a way to diversify by exporting computational power rather than solely oil and gas, anchored by national AI champion **‘Call’**.
* **Corporate Risk and Regulation:**
  * **Jane Fraser:** Described running three simultaneous races at Citi: offense (applying AI to coding and revenue generation), defense (patching infrastructure against advanced threats like the *mythos* model), and managing security perimeters against AI-enabled cyberattacks.
  * **H.E. Ali bin Ahmed Al-Kuwari:** Stressed the urgent need for AI regulation to prevent severe risks, noting recent AI-enabled cyberattacks in London.

## Sovereign Debt, Fiscal Prudence, and Global Divergence
* **Developed Market Fiscal Pressures:**
  * **Emmanuel Roman:** Pointed to looming defining election and bond market cycles in Europe (notably **2027 in France**) and heavy debt loads in the UK and Europe, contrasting them favorably with growth opportunities in the Middle East and Far East.
  * **Jane Fraser:** Noted that while there is marginal diversification away from U.S. assets as global fragmentation increases, the U.S. dollar and Treasuries still lack strong alternatives. She also highlighted the growing global competitiveness of Chinese companies.
* **Fiscal Philosophy:**
  * **H.E. Ali bin Ahmed Al-Kuwari:** Argued that fiscal discipline must be the absolute #1 rule for any government to avoid being crushed by debt-servicing costs during periods of high inflation and interest rates.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **H.E. Ali bin Ahmed Al-Kuwari:** Qatar’s economic contraction will be a V-shaped recovery, compensating for all current GDP losses in **next year**, and positioning Qatar as the fastest-growing economy in the region for the **following 50 years**.
* **Emmanuel Roman:** The US 10-year Treasury yield will experience a release and rates will go down once a better outcome or deal is reached in the Middle East.

## Notable Quotes
> *"If you are fiscal strong, you can do everything, but if you are fiscally weak, you cannot do anything. You cannot even support the economy."* — **H.E. Ali bin Ahmed Al-Kuwari**

> *"The need in terms of capital and in terms of borrowing are like nothing we have ever seen in our career. But also the opportunity is incredible."* — **Emmanuel Roman**

> *"When mythos came out, that was not a good day... there is a tsunami of patching going on in the world at the moment."* — **Jane Fraser**

briefings.title: QatarEnergy on Energy Security and Supply

people.name: Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi
people.role: Minister of State for Energy Affairs, Qatar

briefings.tldr: QatarEnergy is navigating an unprecedented total shutdown of its oil and gas facilities due to disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz, cutting 17% of its LNG capacity.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
QatarEnergy is navigating an unprecedented total shutdown of its oil and gas facilities due to disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz, cutting 17% of its LNG capacity. Despite project delays and force majeure declarations, the company remains committed to regional diplomacy, long-term expansion, and cementing its status as the world's leading LNG trader.

## Impact of the Strait of Hormuz Crisis on Production and Exports
- **Damage Assessment:** Hit to three facilities at Ras Laffan—two LNG trains and one GTL train.
- **Export Limitations:** Only very sparse shipments are exiting through the Strait (some via an Iranian route to Pakistan and a US route), yielding volumes so low they are statistically unmeasurable as a percentage point.
- **Supply Chain Bottlenecks:** Large prefabricated industrial modules (some 50m by 50m) manufactured in Asia cannot be tugged through the Strait, causing delays for expansion projects.

## Pipeline Alternatives and Regional Relations
- **Pipeline Rejection:** Economic and technical studies evaluated alternative pipeline routes through Syria, Yanbu (Saudi Arabia), Fujairah (UAE), and Oman. QatarEnergy decided against them because transporting natural gas via pipeline would require building redundant liquefaction terminals outside Qatar.
- **Long-term Peace:** Minister Al-Kaabi emphasized the necessity of peaceful coexistence with neighbors like Iran for future generations, aiming to build lasting economic ties that outlast hostilities.
- **Strait Longevity:** Al-Kaabi disputed suggestions by US officials that the Strait of Hormuz could become an obsolete waterway within two years, noting it is essential for the trade and survival of numerous Gulf nations.

## Ras Laffan Repairs and Global Market Impacts
- **Repair Timeline:** GTL train repairs are expected to finish by **Q1 2027**; the two LNG trains are targeted for return within **the next three years** (accelerated from an initial 3-to-5-year estimate by working directly with sole closed-box manufacturer FCI). Operations can return to normal within a couple of weeks once the Strait reopens.
- **Contractual Status:** All long-term Sales and Purchase Agreements (SPAs) are tied to force majeure clauses linked to specific trains, meaning QatarEnergy has no obligation to make up lost volumes from alternative global locations.
- **Global Energy Demand:** Unseasonably hot European summers have driven up cooling demand and power usage, depleting European reserves and threatening higher winter prices if the weather is harsh.

## International Projects and Trading Ambitions
- **Global Trading Expansion:** QatarEnergy aims to become **the largest LNG trader in the world by far** in the very near future, building upon the massive trading organization established in 2024.
- **US and Global Assets:** 
  - **Golden Pass (US):** First train has started shipments; both second and third trains are expected in full operation next year.
  - **Golden Triangle (US):** The world's largest ethane cracker (a joint venture with Chevron Phillips, where QatarEnergy owns 49%) is beginning commissioning and will start up in the coming weeks.
  - **Exploration:** Active in global exploration blocks including Namibia, Cyprus, Angola, Brazil, Argentina, and the US, with serious evaluations underway regarding potential entry into Venezuela.
- **Domestic Expansion Status:** North Field East (NFE) construction is proceeding well, with the first train expected to come online in the **first half of next year**, followed by North Field South (NFS) trains, though ongoing Strait access issues could cause localized delays.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **GTL Facility Restoration:** The damaged GTL train will be fully repaired by **the first quarter of 2027** — Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi.
- **LNG Train Restoration Timeline:** The two damaged LNG trains will be back into operation **within the next three years** (brought forward from an initial 3-to-5-year estimate) — Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi.
- **Global LNG Trading Dominance:** QatarEnergy will become **the largest LNG trader in the world by far** in the very near future — Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi.
- **Golden Pass Full Operation:** Both the second and third trains at the Golden Pass facility will be in **full operation next year** — Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi.
- **Golden Triangle Startup:** The Golden Triangle ethane cracker will start up **in the next few weeks** — Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi.
- **North Field East Milestone:** The first train of the North Field East expansion will come online **in the first half of next year** — Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi.
- **Market Glut Outlook:** A supply glut of LNG is expected in **2027 and 2028** due to incoming US and global volumes, provided Qatar goes back online — Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi.

## Notable Quotes
> "I think to have a complete shutdown of all our oil and gas facilities and petrochemicals and all the host of things that we produce, and all of them to come down to zero and one go is unprecedented, not only in Qatar, but in any, uh, country that produces oil and gas."
> — **H.E. Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi**

> "We have decided not to do pipelines... The decision in Qatar was based on commercial and technical, and we are only going to be using the Straits."
> — **H.E. Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi**

> "Iran is going to be there for, uh, you know, uh, to live with my grandkids and their grandkids. And we're in one region. We need to all get along together and have some kind of an understanding that we can all live peacefully."
> — **H.E. Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi**

> "I would like to mention today that we will be in the very near future. The largest LNG trader in the world is by far. And we are building our position to become the largest trader."
> — **H.E. Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi**

briefings.title: Steven Mnuchin Sees Long-Term Opportunity in Middle East
briefings.tldr: Former Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin says Middle East investment faces short-term uncertainty from the Iran conflict but remains attractive long-term under Trump's leadership, while backing strict enforcement of Iran sanctions, potential action against Chinese banks, and a broader AI understanding with China.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Former Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin says Middle East investment faces short-term uncertainty from the Iran conflict but remains attractive long-term under Trump's leadership, while backing strict enforcement of Iran sanctions, potential action against Chinese banks, and a broader AI understanding with China.

## Middle East Investment & Geopolitical Conflict
* **Short-Term Uncertainty vs. Long-Term Potential:** 
  * Short-term investment in the Middle East is currently on hold due to the ongoing conflict involving Iran and disruptions to LNG supply in Qatar.
  * Long-Term Outlook: Bringing the Middle East together, advancing the Abraham Accords between Israel and its Arab neighbors, and regional economic diversification efforts are positive long-term drivers.
* **Energy Security & American Leadership:** 
  * Free access through the strait must be restored; American leadership and potential military involvement can ensure open traffic and resolve the situation.

## US Treasury & Monetary Policy
* **Assessment of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent:** 
  * Bessent is performing terrifically, particularly in leading critical discussions on China, Iran, and AI.
  * Bond Buybacks: The buyback program originated under Janet Yellen and was activated by Bessent, but issuance strategy is a more critical focus.
  * Borrowing Approach: It would be reasonable to shift toward more short-term borrowing and less long-term borrowing on the margin given rising interest rates.
  * Currency Interventions: Bessent's intervention approach—supporting Japan—differs from Mnuchin's fundamentalist trading style.
* **Federal Reserve Leadership & Rates:** 
  * Support for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh: Warsh is a great leader, but should pause rate hikes for now.
  * Core Inflation & Energy Shocks: Core inflation is improving, but energy shocks heavily influence current economic conditions; raising rates immediately ahead of an election would be inappropriate.
  * Forward Guidance: Warsh is right to abandon dot plots, as predicting rates a year or two out is unreliable; market signaling should instead happen via speeches.

## US-China Relations, Trade, & AI
* **Economic Dialogue & China's Structural Challenges:** 
  * Treasury secretaries must remain front and center in the US-China economic relationship, continuing the precedent set by Hank Paulson.
  * China's Economic Position: China faces severe demographic challenges, including an aging population and a projected population shrinkage of hundreds of millions.
* **Artificial Intelligence Guardrails:** 
  * Domestic Consensus: The US must first establish a domestic mechanism and consensus on AI guardrails, aided by the newly created AI force and industry leaders.
  * Bilateral Understanding: The US and China are "frenemies"; AI must be included in high-level discussions alongside nuclear issues, similar to how China cooperated on North Korea during Trump's first term.

## Sanctions & Economic Statecraft
* **Effectiveness of Sanctions:** 
  * Economic sanctions are highly effective due to the US dollar's status as the world's reserve currency, though they require careful use and strict enforcement.
  * Past Success: During Trump's first term, maximum sanctions against Iran worked successfully, prompting multiple requests from Iran to negotiate because the global community cooperated.
  * Contrast with Biden Administration: Russian sanctions under President Biden failed because they lacked enforcement and prioritized domestic gas prices.
* **China Compliance & Enforcement:** 
  * China must be part of the solution on Iran; if China fails to cooperate, the US should apply strong sanctions and lock out Chinese banks from the US dollar system.

## Notable Quotes
> *"The strait is open and will be open and that [Iran] can't hold it hostage. So I think there's no question that invest short term investment on the moment is obviously on hold, but, I I believe this issue longer term will all be a lot safer with president Trump dealing with Iran and the nuclear issue."* — Steven Mnuchin

> *"The dollar is the reserve currency of the world. I always said with that comes huge advantages and huge responsibilities. And because sanctions are so effective, we have to be careful how we use them."* — Steven Mnuchin

> *"I think he positioned himself ahead of the last meeting that, you know, he made it very clear if the inflation numbers didn't weren't coming in, he was gonna raise. So I think he had no choice. He had to raise. Having said that, if if I were Fed chair, I would make it clear that things are on hold for now."* — Steven Mnuchin

briefings.title: Why the People Who Built Hip-Hop Ended Up With Nothing

people.name: Nas
people.role: Rapper and Co-founder, Paid in Full Foundation

briefings.tldr: The Paid in Full Foundation pairs financial grants with deep personal recognition to honor and support the foundational pioneers of hip-hop who built a multi-billion dollar culture while capturing almost none of its wealth.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
The Paid in Full Foundation pairs financial grants with deep personal recognition to honor and support the foundational pioneers of hip-hop who built a multi-billion dollar culture while capturing almost none of its wealth. Founded by Ben Horowitz, Steve Stoute, and Nas alongside Felicia Horowitz, the initiative fosters genuine community, healing, and cross-generational connection among hip-hop legends.

## Origins and Mission of the Paid in Full Foundation
* **Foundational Inspiration:** Ben Horowitz was inspired to start the foundation because he purchased the album *Paid in Full* for $10 and derived at least $5 million in career value from it, feeling a pressing need to pay that value back.
* **The Core Problem:** 
  * **Financial Disconnect:** Artists poured immense creativity into culture—changing fashion, dialect, and lifestyle brands like Tommy Hilfiger and Adidas—while their bank accounts and acknowledgments remained empty.
  * **Industry Division:** The music industry historically separated artists by success, status, old school versus new school, and competitiveness, creating an every-man-for-yourself culture.
* **Nas's Insight on Delivery:** When consulted, Nas noted that simply handing out money wouldn't work in hip-hop because artists would view it as charity or reparations; the support had to be paired with profound public honor, dignity, and celebration.
* **The Grandmaster Awards:** Created to honor true greats, the foundation initially faced widespread disbelief, with some artists rejecting the calls or awards because they thought it was a scam due to decades of industry mistreatment.

## Impact and Personal Stories from the Pioneers
* **Grandmaster Caz:** Wrote the rhymes that became "Rapper's Delight" (with his name in the lyrics), which was stolen from him without proper credit or reward.
  * **Life Transformation:** Receiving the 5-year grant allowed him to buy a house in Pennsylvania, move out of the Bronx projects, escape the day-to-day grind, and eliminate his fear of dying in the projects.
  * **Ongoing Hustle:** Emphasized that hip-hop lacks social security or health benefits, forcing pioneers to keep working park jams and tours to survive.
* **Scarface & Medical Crises:** Scarface needed a kidney transplant and open-heart surgery, but was initially in complete shock when Ben Horowitz called him from the South of France to cover his medical needs.
  * **Felicia's Intervention:** Felicia Horowitz personally flew to Houston and insisted Scarface go to the doctor, saving his life just as his aorta burst on the way in.
* **Roxanne Shanté:** Her child asked if she felt bitter seeing new female rappers win awards; she replied that she didn't want those awards—she wanted the *Paid in Full* award.
* **Cross-Generational Bonding:** At foundation events, multi-platinum icons like Dr. Dre requested introductions to legends like Slick Rick and Kurtis Blow, whom they had never met despite decades in the industry.

## Scaling, Funding, and the Annual Gala
* **Matching Model:** Ben and Felicia Horowitz match every donation 2.5 to 1.
* **Volunteer Operation:** There are zero paid employees at the foundation; 100% of donated funds go directly to the artists and grants.
* **The Gala Experience:** 
  * Described as feeling like a joyful family reunion with zero egos, deep mutual respect, and unscripted park-jam performances.
  * Past highlights include George Clinton (age 83) reciting Rakim's "Follow the Leader" lyrics on stage, and Ice Cube declaring he never dropped an album without first listening to Scarface.
* **The Quincy Jones Award:** Created in direct response to the Grammys mishandling Quincy Jones's tribute; this year's recipient is Nile Rogers (producer of Chic, Sister Sledge, and Daft Punk's "Get Lucky").

## Notable Quotes
> *"Hip-hop don't have social security. You have to work. You got to stay out there."* — **Grandmaster Caz**

> *"I think in life it's impossible to do anything great if you start with what's possible. You have to start with what's right."* — **Ben Horowitz**

> *"My the last thoughts in my head for the last like 10 15 years [were]: I don't want to die in the projects. I don't want to end here."* — **Grandmaster Caz**
